## Cross-examination, read blind

**The strongest falsifiable claim on the bench** is Seat C's reference-class statement: names above 24 times forward earnings with about 11 percent guided growth mostly lag the index over three years. It is checkable and it is doing real work.

**Blind spots, by seat.** Seat A treats a repeated guidance range as delivery; repetition is the norm before cuts too, as Seat C notes, and Seat A never engages that. Seat B quotes the short-sale reading to six decimal places without saying what would make the shorts right. Seat D concedes its squeeze case cannot be scored and should have stopped there rather than gesturing at it. Seat E is the most disciplined: it prices the gap risk instead of narrating it.

**What all five missed:** nobody asked what the risk-free rate reading being stale does to the yield comparison; the pack flags it and no seat priced it.

No seat named itself or another seat. No writing-rule lapses to flag: no unexplained case terms or uncommon acronyms on the bench.
synopsis: Five lenses, one agreement: the growth story is real and the price already carries it. The bull leans on a repeated guidance range; the skeptic answers with the reference class, where ratings this full mostly disappoint over three years. The bear adds an elevated short-sale reading with no scoreable borrow cost. The risk lens is the most useful: drawdowns here arrive as results-day gaps, so the case is about the next print, not the next quarter of drift. The one shared blind spot is the stale risk-free reading, which no seat priced into the yield comparison. Nothing on the bench argues for paying today; everything argues for named triggers and patience.
